gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-imperial: Rugged, vintage swagger up front. Woodgod's wide-channeled bowls and lowercase nearly touching the capitals sit against Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic, a plain sans whose c ends point apart like pincers.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kharosht: Loud, vintage, and entirely sure of itself. Woodgod's wide-channeled bowls command the top, while Noto Sans Kharoshthi sets down a dense, dark stripe of sans-serif lowercase with curves that stay open.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Vintage muscle, then a quiet reply. Woodgod is built to command attention with its wide-channeled bowls, while Noto Sans Khudawadi, a plain sans with unsealed rounds, is built to be read.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Vintage swagger, built to be noticed. Woodgod does the shouting, and Noto Sans Old Italic, a plain sans with curve endings held well apart, would read smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-numans: Big vintage presence, right at the top. What stands out most is the pull between Woodgod's commanding, wide-channeled bowls and Numans, a plain sans whose tracking is pushed well past normal.
gen-gf-mali-fs-recia: Doodled warmth meets a sharper hand. Mali's relaxed, handwritten letters loosen things up, then Recia, a text serif whose modulation is light, steps in to keep a few lines feeling grounded.
